# Ambrose Tuscano

> Software engineer: backend, cloud and distributed systems, with production agentic-AI experience. Software Engineer II at Microsoft on Azure Resource Graph (12B+ Azure resources a day); previously Sr. Generative AI Engineer at Nissan and Software Engineer at Amazon Ads. Open to backend engineering, cloud engineering, distributed systems and platform engineering, data infrastructure, and AI/agentic systems engineering roles.

Core expertise: distributed systems design, high-throughput data pipelines, serverless architecture, API development and modeling, ML/AI integration, infrastructure and performance optimization, real-time event-driven systems, observability, multi-agent system design, and prompt engineering.

Highlights, all from the resume:
- Microsoft: Azure Resource Graph; a five-region scale-out that roughly doubled capacity with no added cloud spend; a new-region buildout; pipeline observability.
- Nissan: designed and shipped Tell Me More, a production four-agent system on AWS Bedrock AgentCore.
- Amazon Ads: Ad Relevance API launch (over 1M TPS); APIs under 15 ms at 1,000+ TPS; real-time evaluation at 5K+ TPS; a data pipeline taken from 17M to 52M products a day; a 5x-throughput labeling service.
- M.S. in Computer Science, University of Maryland, Baltimore County.

## Writing

Long-form technical posts, each with interactive diagrams and a narrated video:

- [First in Line](https://tascano.github.io/notes/first-in-line.html): a local, single-user job-hunting agent; ATS feed adapters with exact timestamps, computer-use discovery on LinkedIn and Google at human pace, dedupe with three SQLite stores (source ID + fingerprint), rules-then-model matching with caching, form filling via field mappings then computer use, intent-before-submit idempotency, its own inbox for verification and replies, an outreach skill, fairness caps
- [Seven O'Clock, Every Morning](https://tascano.github.io/notes/seven-oclock-every-morning.html): Daily Bible as eleven microservices, tested with docker compose then moved to AWS; every subscriber flow, idempotent runs, per-time-zone fan-out, pacing, circuit breakers, an outbox, a fallback ladder; sign-up surges, trials and Stripe webhook ordering, bounces and complaints, multi-tenant fair queuing, millisecond-aligned sends, failure modes and cost levers
- [The File That Wouldn't Die](https://tascano.github.io/notes/file-that-wouldnt-die.html): a peer-to-peer file system grown from one laptop to the internet; TCP framing, consistent hashing, quorums, gossip, Merkle trees, erasure coding, Raft
- [The Teammate in My Terminal](https://tascano.github.io/notes/teammate-in-my-terminal.html): the Claude Code setup (rules, skills, allow lists, hooks) behind his posts and videos
- [Four Agents Walk Into a Service Bay](https://tascano.github.io/notes/agents-service-bay.html): designing a multi-agent intake system for scale, speed, reliability, visibility and failover (his own recreation, not Nissan's system)
- [A Million Questions a Second](https://tascano.github.io/notes/scaling-ad-relevance-apis.html): an ad-relevance API at over a million requests a second; precompute, Bloom filters, fan-out, SNS/SQS pipelines, failover (numbers illustrative)
- [The Terminal Was Always a Log](https://tascano.github.io/notes/the-terminal-was-always-a-log.html): terminal internals, PTYs, and terminals as distributed systems

## Video series

- [Systems on Glass](https://tascano.github.io/series/): an AI-automation side project; episodes generated by Claude (via Claude Code) from the owner's stories and reviewed by the owner; one system-design or AI-engineering idea a day, drawn simply (system design Mon/Wed/Fri, AI agents Tue/Thu/Sat, AI at scale on Sunday)
- [Episode 1: Latency vs Throughput](https://tascano.github.io/series/latency-vs-throughput.html): two problems, two fixes; Little's law, queueing delay at high utilisation, Prime Day headroom, tail latency under fan-out; with further reading
- [Episode 2: What Is an Agent?](https://tascano.github.io/series/what-is-an-agent.html): an agent is a model in a loop (think, act with a tool, observe, check); tools as hands; goal, budget and human-in-the-loop as stopping conditions; with further reading
- [Episode 3: Caching](https://tascano.github.io/series/caching.html): hits and misses, cache-aside and read-through, write-through/behind/around, hit-rate maths, lazy versus eager (weekly precompute), HTTP caching, LRU/LFU/TTL and Belady, learned caching, invalidation, herds and coalescing; then AI caching: KV cache, prompt caching, response and semantic caches, agent-side content-keyed caches; with further reading
- [Episode 4: Context Is RAM](https://tascano.github.io/series/context-is-ram.html): the context window as RAM; lost in the middle (Liu et al.), context rot (Chroma), token cost per step; what Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI and Microsoft Research say about long context and where to put the question; four memory moves (load late, compact, write it down, fork); with further reading
- [Episode 5: Indexes](https://tascano.github.io/series/indexes.html): full scan vs index, binary search, B-trees (Bayer and McCreight, 1970) and four page reads, hash, inverted, vector (HNSW) and LSM indexes, write costs, selectivity, column order, expression and covering indexes, and the owner's Amazon Ads API: point lookups by key, DynamoDB hash partitioning and hot keys, a Bloom filter, global secondary indexes; plus an illustration, from Microsoft's public docs, of how a cloud-scale index like Azure Resource Graph is kept current (not its internal design); with further reading
- [Episode 6: Prompt Like a Spec](https://tascano.github.io/series/prompt-like-a-spec.html): why the best prompt is a spec, not clever wording; vague prompts and literal models (OpenAI GPT-4.1 and GPT-5 guides, Anthropic Claude docs, Google Gemini docs); the five parts of a spec (goal and why, inputs, rules, output, done when) with examples from the owner's own AI video studio (its CLAUDE.md and the Daily Bible rule "never invent or paraphrase scripture"); Sean Grove's "The New Code"; GitHub Spec Kit, Kiro and AGENTS.md; the page carries the vertical Short, the full video is on YouTube
- [Episode 7: What an LLM Call Costs](https://tascano.github.io/series/llm-call-costs.html): tokens in and out priced separately, output about five times input (Anthropic and OpenAI list prices, Nov 2026), a receipt for one call, the agent loop where re-sending the conversation dominates the bill, and how prompt caching, batch APIs, smaller models and shorter answers cut it; illustrative arithmetic, labelled; the page carries the vertical Short, the full video is on YouTube
- [Episode 8: Queues](https://tascano.github.io/series/queues.html): why the owner's Daily Bible 7 AM send starts at 6:00; the naive loop (80/s, 1 h 44 min for half a million, illustrative), freezing the list into shards before firing, pacing with a token bucket under the provider's limit, more lanes for throughput (40 × 250/s: 50 s), lanes that keep WhatsApp, email and codes apart, scaling before a known spike, and retries, a dead-letter queue and a sweeper; the page carries the vertical Short, the full video is on YouTube
- [Episode 9: Give Your Agent a Memory](https://tascano.github.io/series/agent-memory.html): the owner's agent ran out of context mid-episode, compacted and kept going because what mattered lived in files; the four kinds of agent memory from Princeton's CoALA paper (working, semantic, episodic, procedural), CLAUDE.md loaded at every launch and written concrete enough to verify, corrections written down as rules, notes the agent keeps (Anthropic's Claude playing Pokémon, the memory tool), skills opened just in time, compaction, and keeping each memory file under 200 lines; sources on screen; the page carries the vertical Short, the full video is on YouTube
- [Episode 10: Retries, Backoff and Jitter](https://tascano.github.io/series/retries-backoff-jitter.html): when the owner's Daily Bible sends fail at once, why retrying right away repeats the wave; retries multiplying in a deep stack (243x, Amazon Builders' Library); AWS's October 2025 us-east-1 'congestive collapse'; exponential backoff and why it still moves in waves; full jitter from Marc Brooker's 2015 post to AWS's 2026 SDK defaults (random(0,1) x min(20 s, base x 2^retry), 3 attempts, a 500-token retry quota); never retrying a permanent failure; 429 Retry-After; dead letters after five tries; the page carries the vertical Short, the full video is on YouTube
- [Episode 11: Skills](https://tascano.github.io/series/skills.html): agent skills from the owner's own video-studio skill (34 files, 205,859 characters, 893 loaded at startup); a skill as a folder with SKILL.md; progressive disclosure in three levels (the label, the steps, the tools); the description as the trigger; scripts run without being read into context; a skill that keeps learning; the open standard at agentskills.io (Dec 2025); install only from trusted sources; sources: Anthropic's Agent Skills post (Oct 2025) and the Claude Code docs; the page carries the vertical Short, the full video is on YouTube
- [Episode 12: Idempotency](https://tascano.github.io/series/idempotency.html): from the owner's JobHunt agent, which crashed mid-submit; once or ten times the same result; why a timeout tells you nothing; idempotency keys (same key, saved answer; fresh key, a duplicate); the IETF Idempotency-Key header draft-08 (Oct 2026) and Stripe's idempotent requests; writing the intent before the work (status = applying, then check the site and inbox before a retry); keying the thing, not the message (one job, five IDs, a fingerprint); keys expire (Stripe 24 h), 409 and 422; the page carries the vertical Short, the full video is on YouTube
- [Episode 13: Stop Babysitting](https://tascano.github.io/series/stop-babysitting.html): permissions for an AI agent in Claude Code, from the owner's studio: allow, ask and deny rules; 46 allow rules for free commands; a hole found while making the episode (a free rule that also matched the paid 'images --yes') and the fix (rules are checked deny, then ask, then allow; one ask rule on --yes); deny rules for .env files; rules match commands, not intentions ('fragile'); sandboxing (84% fewer prompts, Anthropic, Oct 2025) and auto mode; the page carries the vertical Short, the full video is on YouTube
- [Episode 14: Cache the Model](https://tascano.github.io/series/cache-the-model.html): an investigation into two caches for AI models, from the owner's studio (an episode rendered four times, its voice paid once: a response cache keyed by sha256 of the words and settings); the prompt cache (Anthropic: write 1.25x, read 0.1x, 0.05x on Opus 5.5, 5-minute or 1-hour lifetime; OpenAI: automatic above 1,024 tokens, up to 95% off); what breaks it (one changed word near the top; the clock); when not to cache an answer; the page carries the vertical Short, the full video is on YouTube
